questions.q: What are the four parts of a four-part name?
options: server.database.schema.object
database.schema.object.column
provider.server.database.object
server.instance.database.schema
questions.explain: A four-part name is server.database.schema.object, adding the linked server name in front of the familiar three-part local naming.

questions.q: Where does the query text inside an OPENQUERY call actually execute?
options: Entirely on the remote server, using its own optimizer, indexes, and statistics
On the local server, then sent to the remote server for storage
It never executes — OPENQUERY only returns cached metadata
Half on the local server and half on the remote server, always split evenly
questions.explain: OPENQUERY passes its query string through as-is to be executed entirely on the remote server, and only the result set crosses the network.

questions.q: What is a real performance risk of using a four-part name for a query with a filtering WHERE clause on the remote table?
options: The local optimizer may not push the filter down efficiently, pulling more rows across the network than necessary
Four-part names are always slower than OPENQUERY in every case with no exceptions
Four-part names cannot use WHERE clauses at all
Four-part names automatically disable the remote server's indexes
questions.explain: With four-part naming, the local optimizer decides how much work happens remotely, and it doesn't always push predicates down efficiently, unlike OPENQUERY which forces remote-side execution.

questions.q: For a query doing heavy filtering and aggregation against a large remote table, which approach is generally more efficient?
options: OPENQUERY, because it pushes the whole query to run remotely and only returns the already-reduced result set
Four-part naming, because it is always faster regardless of query shape
Neither approach can filter on the remote side
It makes no difference which approach is used
questions.explain: OPENQUERY forces execution on the remote server using its own optimizer, which is typically more efficient for queries that need substantial remote-side filtering or aggregation.

questions.q: What is a downside of OPENQUERY compared to a four-part name?
options: The inner query is just a string that SQL Server doesn't parse or validate against local metadata
OPENQUERY cannot be used with a linked server at all
OPENQUERY always returns more rows than requested
OPENQUERY requires disabling the linked server's login mapping
questions.explain: OPENQUERY trades away some syntactic convenience and local validation since its query text is an opaque string executed remotely, unlike the T-SQL-native four-part name syntax.
